evidence.pali: 373 . ‘‘Katamañcāvuso, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Jātipi dukkhā, jarāpi dukkhā, maraṇampi dukkhaṃ, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsāpi dukkhā, yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ; saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā.
evidence.chinese_simplified: 373. “贤友们，什么是苦圣谛？生是苦，老是苦，死是苦，愁、悲、苦、忧、恼亦是苦，所求不得亦是苦；简言之，五取蕴是苦。”
evidence.english: 373. “And what, friends, is the noble truth of suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are suffering; not to get what one wants is also suffering; in short, the five aggregates subject to clinging are suffering.

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: ‘Anūnādhikato’ ti kasmā pana cattāreva ariyasaccāni vuttāni, anūnāni anadhikānīti ce? Aññassāsambhavato, aññatarassa ca anapaneyyabhāvato; na hi etehi aññaṃ adhikaṃ vā etesaṃ vā ekampi apanetabbaṃ sambhoti. Yathāha – ‘‘idha, bhikkhave, āgaccheyya samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā ‘netaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, aññaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ yaṃ samaṇena gotamena desitaṃ. Ahametaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paññapessāmī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’tiādi. Yathā cāha – ‘‘yo hi koci, bhikkhave, samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃ vadeyya ‘netaṃ dukkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, yaṃ samaṇena gotamena desitaṃ. Ahametaṃ dukkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paccakkhāya aññaṃ dukkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paññapessāmī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’tiādi (saṃ. ni. 5.1086).
entries.chinese_simplified: “不多不少”者何？何故只说四圣谛，不多不少耶？因无其他，亦不可减一。于此等之外，实不可能增一，亦不可能减一。正如世尊所说：“诸比丘，若有沙门或婆罗门来，作如是言：‘沙门乔达摩(Gotama)所说者，非是苦圣谛。我将舍此苦圣谛，另立一苦圣谛。’此事无有是处。”又如所说：“诸比丘，若有任何沙门或婆罗门作如是言：‘沙门乔达摩所说者，非是第一苦圣谛。我将否定此第一苦圣谛，另立一第一苦圣谛。’此事无有是处。”（《相应部》5.1086）
entries.english: As to 'neither deficient nor excessive,' why are only four Noble Truths stated, neither deficient nor excessive? Because no other is possible, and none of them can be removed. Indeed, nothing more can arise beyond them, nor can even a single one be taken away from them. As it is said: 'Here, bhikkhus, if any ascetic or brahmin were to come and say, "This is not the Noble Truth of Suffering taught by the ascetic Gotama; setting aside this Noble Truth of Suffering, I will designate another Noble Truth of Suffering," such a thing is impossible,' and so on. And as it is further said: 'Bhikkhus, if any ascetic or brahmin were to say, "This is not the first Noble Truth of Suffering taught by the ascetic Gotama; rejecting this first Noble Truth of Suffering, I will designate another first Noble Truth of Suffering," such a thing is impossible,' and so on (SN 5.1086).

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: 190 . Idāni saṅkhepato uddiṭṭhāni dukkhādīni vibhajitvā dassetuṃ ayaṃ tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ jātipi dukkhā ti niddesavāro āraddho. Tattha jāti veditabbā, jātiyā dukkhaṭṭho veditabbo; jarā, maraṇaṃ, soko , paridevo, dukkhaṃ, domanassaṃ, upāyāso, appiyasampayogo, piyavippayogo veditabbo; appiyasampayogassa piyavippayogassa dukkhaṭṭho veditabbo; icchā veditabbā, icchāya dukkhaṭṭho veditabbo; khandhā veditabbā, khandhānaṃ dukkhaṭṭho veditabbo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 190. 现在，为分别开示略说之苦等，开启此“其中，何为苦圣谛？生亦是苦”之解释章。于此，应知生，应知生之苦义；应知老、死、愁、悲、苦、忧、恼、怨憎会、爱别离；应知怨憎会与爱别离之苦义；应知欲求，应知欲求之苦义；应知诸蕴，应知诸蕴之苦义。
entries.english: 190. Now, to explain in detail what has been stated concisely—namely, suffering and so on—this section of exposition on “what, therein, is the Noble Truth of Suffering? Birth is suffering” is begun. Herein, birth should be understood, and the nature of suffering in birth should be understood. Aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, despair, association with the disliked, and separation from the liked—these should be understood. The nature of suffering in association with the disliked and separation from the liked should be understood. Desire should be understood, and the nature of suffering in desire should be understood. The aggregates should be understood, and the nature of suffering in the aggregates should be understood.

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: Tattha pariyāyadukkhaṃ nippariyāyadukkhanti imasmiṃ padadvaye ṭhatvā dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ kathetabbaṃ. Ariyasaccañca nāmetaṃ pāḷiyaṃ saṅkhepatopi āgacchati vitthāratopi. Saṅkhepato āgataṭṭhāne saṅkhepenapi vitthārenapi kathetuṃ vaṭṭati . Vitthārato āgataṭṭhāne pana vitthāreneva kathetuṃ vaṭṭati, na saṅkhepena. Taṃ idaṃ imasmiṃ ṭhāne vitthārena āgatanti vitthāreneva kathetabbaṃ. Tasmā yaṃ taṃ niddesavāre ‘‘tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Jātipi dukkhā’’tiādīni padāni gahetvā ‘‘jāti veditabbā, jātiyā dukkhaṭṭho veditabbo’’tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha jātiādīni tāva ‘‘tattha katamā jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jāti sañjātī’’ti imassa pana padabhājanīyassa vasena veditabbāni.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于此，应依“方便苦”与“非方便苦”此二词宣说苦圣谛。此圣谛在圣典中，既有略说，亦有广说。于略说处，可略说亦可广说；然于广说处，则只应广说，不应略说。此处于此是广说，故应广说。是故，于解释章中，引用“其中，何为苦圣谛？生亦是苦”等句，并言“应知生，应知生之苦义”等。其中，生等，当依“其中，何为生？即于彼彼众生部类中，彼彼众生之生、发生”此一句之分别来了知。
entries.english: Here, having established these two terms—suffering by implication and suffering without implication—the Noble Truth of Suffering should be explained. And this Noble Truth occurs in the Pāli texts both in brief and in detail. Where it occurs briefly, it is suitable to explain it both concisely and elaborately. But where it occurs in detail, it is suitable to explain it only in detail, not concisely. Since it occurs in detail in this place, it must be explained in detail. Therefore, in the section of exposition, taking the phrases such as, “Therein, what is the Noble Truth of Suffering? Birth is suffering,” and so on, it is said, “Birth should be understood, the nature of suffering in birth should be understood,” and so forth. There, first, birth and the like should be understood according to the analysis of the phrase: “Therein, what is birth? It is the birth, the coming-to-be, of those various beings in those various classes of beings.”

entries.pali: 190 . Tattha …pe… ayaṃ mātikā ti niddesavāraādimhi vutte jātiādiniddese tesaṃ jātiādīnaṃ niddesavasena dukkhassa ariyasaccassa kathanatthāya, tesu vā jātiādīsu tesañca dukkhaṭṭhe veditabbe jātiādīnaṃ niddesavasena dukkhassa ariyasaccassa kathanatthāya dukkhadukkhantiādikā dukkhamātikā veditabbāti attho. Atha vā tatthā ti tasmiṃ niddesavāre. ‘‘Jātipi dukkhā…pe… saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā’’ti ayaṃ dukkhassa ariyasaccassa kathanatthāya mātikāti yathādassitassa jātiādiniddesassa mātikābhāvaṃ dīpeti. Taṃ dīpetvā puna yasmiṃ padadvaye ṭhatvā dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ kathetabbaṃ, tassa niddhāraṇatthaṃ sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ saṅkaḍḍhento āha ‘‘idañhi dukkhaṃ nāmā’’ tiādi.
entries.chinese_simplified: 190. 在此……此是总纲。在解释章的开头所说的生等解释中，为了以解释生等的方式来说明苦圣谛，或者，在那些生等中，为了在应了知其苦义时，以解释生等的方式来说明苦圣谛，其义是：应了知以‘苦苦’等开头的苦之总纲。又或者，‘在此’是指在该解释章中。‘生亦是苦……简言之，五取蕴是苦’，此为说明苦圣谛的总纲，如此阐明了如前所示的生等解释具有总纲的性质。阐明此后，为了确定应立足于哪两个词来宣说苦圣谛，他总括一切苦而说：‘此即名为苦’等。
entries.english: 190. Herein... this is the matrix. In the section on exposition, at the beginning of the recitation, in the exposition of birth and so on, for the purpose of explaining the Noble Truth of Suffering by way of the exposition of birth and so on; or, with regard to birth and so on, when their nature as suffering is to be understood, for the purpose of explaining the Noble Truth of Suffering by way of the exposition of birth and so on, the matrix of suffering, beginning with 'suffering as suffering,' is to be understood. This is the meaning. Alternatively, 'herein' means in that section on exposition. 'Birth is suffering... in brief, the five aggregates of clinging are suffering'—this is the matrix for the purpose of explaining the Noble Truth of Suffering; thus it clarifies the nature as a matrix of the exposition of birth and so on, as has been shown. Having clarified that, then, in order to determine the two terms upon which the Noble Truth of Suffering is to be explained, drawing together all suffering, he says, 'This, indeed, is called suffering,' and so on.

entries.pali: 1 . Te eva dhamme ti te eva kusalādike tikadukehi saṅgahite dhamme. Suttante khandhādivasena vutte khandhādivasena vibhajitunti yojanā. Nanu suttante paṭisambhidāvasena te na vuttāti? Yadipi sarūpato na vuttā, ‘‘jarāmaraṇe ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇasamudaye ñāṇa’’ntiādinā (saṃ. ni. 2.33) pana hetuhetuphalādīsu ñāṇavibhāgassa vuttattā atthato vuttā eva honti, paṭisambhidāmagge (paṭi. ma. 2.30) vā paṭisambhidānaṃ āgatattā suttante paṭisambhidāvasenapi te dhammā vuttā eva. Tatthā ti tasmiṃ suttante. Saṅkhepenā ti samāsena. Uddesaniddesamatteneva hi suttante khandhādayo desitā, na paṭiniddesādināti saṅkhepena te tattha vuttāti vuttā. Tatthā ti vā dhammasaṅgahe. Tatthāpi hi ‘‘tasmiṃ kho pana samaye cattāro khandhā hontī’’tiādinā (dha. sa. 58) khandhādayo saṅkhepena vuttāti. Vibhajīyanti ettha, etena vā khandhādayoti vibhaṅgo, te eva pakirīyanti paṭṭhapīyanti ettha, etena vāti pakaraṇaṃ, vibhaṅgo ca so pakaraṇañcāti vibhaṅgappakaraṇaṃ. Ādisaddatthajotakenā ti ‘‘iti vā, iti evarūpā naccagītavāditavisūkadassanā paṭivirato’’tiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.13) viya ādisaddassa atthadīpakena. Pakāratthajotakenā ti ‘‘iti kho, bhikkhave, sappaṭibhayo bālo, appaṭibhayo paṇḍito’’tiādīsu (a. ni. 3.1) viya pakāratthavibhāvakena. ‘‘Ekadesena samudāyaṃ nidassetī’’ ti etena ‘‘rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho’’ti ettha itisaddassa nidassanatthataṃ dasseti. Nidassanatthopi hi iti-saddo diṭṭho yathā ‘‘atthīti kho, kaccāna, ayameko anto’’tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 2.15; 3.90). Parisamāpanattho vā ‘‘tasmātiha me, bhikkhave, dhammadāyādā bhavatha, no āmisadāyādā. Atthi me tumhesu anukampā ‘kinti me sāvakā dhammadāyādā bhaveyyuṃ, no āmisadāyādā’ti’’ (ma. ni. 1.29) evamādīsu viya. Parisamāpanañhetaṃ suttantabhājanīyassa ekadesadassanena yadidaṃ ‘‘pañcakkhandhā rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho’’ti tāva tadatthassa saṅgahitattā. Tatthā ti vibhaṅgappakaraṇe. ‘‘Nibbānavajjāna’’ nti ettha yadi nibbānavajjānaṃ…pe… appakatarapadattā khandhānaṃ khandhavibhaṅgo ādimhi vutto, nanu saha nibbānena sabbadhammasaṅgāhakattā, sabbadhammasaṅgāhakehi ca āyatanādīhi khandhehi ca appakatarapadattā saccavibhaṅgo ādimhi vattabboti ? Na, tatthāpi dukkhasaccavibhaṅge ekadesena khandhānaṃ eva vibhajitabbato. Yathāha ‘‘tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Jātipi dukkhā…pe… saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā’’ti (vibha. 190; dī. ni. 2.387; ma. ni. 1.120; 3.373). Idha pana anavasesatova khandhā vibhajīyantīti nibbānavajjānaṃ…pe… appakatarapadattā khandhānaṃ khandhavibhaṅgo ādimhi vutto.
entries.chinese_simplified: 1. “那些法”即那些为善等三法与二法所摄之法。应如是结合：“在经中以蕴等的方式宣说，在此则以蕴等的方式分别。”难道在经中不是以无碍解(paṭisambhidā)的方式宣说它们吗？即使形式上未说，但通过“于老死有智，于老死集有智”等(《相应部》2.33)已宣说了于因、因之果等中的智的分别，故从义理上说，它们已被宣说。或因在《无碍解道》(Paṭisambhidāmagga, 2.30)中已出现无碍解，故在经中也已用无碍解的方式宣说了那些法。“于其中”(tattha)即于那经中。“以简略”(saṅkhepena)即以概括。因为在经中，蕴等仅以标示(uddesa)和解说(niddesa)的方式被开示，而非以详尽解说(paṭiniddesa)等方式，故说它们在那里被简略地宣说。或“于其中”(tattha)即于《法集论》(Dhammasaṅgaṇī)中。因为在那里，蕴等也通过“其时，有四蕴”等(《法集论》58)被简略地宣说。蕴等在此中被分别，或以此分别，故为“分别”(vibhaṅga)。它们在此中被散布、安立，或以此散布、安立，故为“论”(pakaraṇa)。既是“分别”又是“论”，故为《分别论》(Vibhaṅgappakaraṇa)。“以阐明‘等’字之义”(ādisaddatthajotakena)，如在“或如是，他远离观看此等舞蹈、歌唱、音乐、表演”(《长部》Dīgha Nikāya, 1.13)中，是以此阐明“等”字之义。“以阐明方式之义”(pakāratthajotakena)，如在“比丘们，如是，愚人有怖，智者无怖”(《增支部》Aṅguttara Nikāya, 3.1)中，是以此阐明方式之义。通过“以一部分显示全部”(ekadesena samudāyaṃ nidassetī)，他显示了在“色蕴……识蕴”中，“iti”(如是)一词的指示义。指示义的“iti”字亦可见，如“迦旃延(Kaccāna)，‘有’，此为一端”(《相应部》Saṃyutta Nikāya, 2.15; 3.90)。或为总结义(parisamāpanattha)，如在“是故，比丘们，你们当为我的法嗣(dhammadāyāda)，而非食嗣(āmisadāyāda)。我于你们有悲悯：‘如何能令我的弟子们成为法嗣，而非食嗣？’”(《中部》Majjhima Nikāya, 1.29)等中。此亦为总结，因为在经分别(suttantabhājanīya)中，通过“五蕴即色蕴……识蕴”这一部分的展示，其义已被总摄。“于其中”(tattha)即于《分别论》(Vibhaṅgappakaraṇa)中。关于“除涅槃外”(nibbānavajja)，若说因为在除涅槃诸法外，蕴的词句较少，而将蕴分别(khandhavibhaṅga)置于首位，那么，难道不应将谛分别(saccavibhaṅga)置于首位吗？因为它与涅槃一起含摄一切法，并且比含摄一切法的处(āyatana)等和蕴的词句更少。答：不应如此。因为在谛分别中，于苦谛分别(dukkhasaccavibhaṅga)里，也只是分别蕴的一部分而已。如言：“此中，何为苦圣谛(dukkha ariyasacca)？生是苦……简言之，五取蕴(pañcupādānakkhandhā)是苦。”而在此(蕴分别)中，蕴被毫无遗漏地分别，是故，因为在除涅槃诸法外，蕴的词句较少，而将蕴分别置于首位。
entries.english: 1. ‘Those very phenomena’ (te eva dhamme) means those very phenomena included under the categories of wholesome and so forth, in the triads and dyads. The meaning is that when the aggregates and so on are mentioned in the discourses, they are to be analyzed in terms of the aggregates and so on. But are they not mentioned in the discourses in terms of the analytical knowledges? Even if not explicitly stated in their own form, they are indeed mentioned in meaning, as seen in phrases like ‘knowledge of aging-and-death, knowledge of the origin of aging-and-death’ (Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.33), where the divisions of knowledge regarding cause, effect, and so on are stated. Alternatively, since the analytical knowledges are included in the Paṭisambhidāmagga (Paṭisambhidāmagga 2.30), these phenomena are indeed mentioned in the discourses in terms of the analytical knowledges. ‘There’ (tattha) means in that discourse. ‘Briefly’ (saṅkhepena) means in summary. For in the discourses, the aggregates and so on are taught merely by way of brief statement and explanation, not by detailed analysis—thus, they are said to be stated there in brief. Or, ‘there’ (tattha) means in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī. For there too, the aggregates and so on are stated briefly, as in: ‘At that time, there are four aggregates’ (Dhammasaṅgaṇī 58). ‘Vibhajīyanti’ (they are analyzed) means that here or by this the aggregates and so on are analyzed; this is the Vibhaṅga. ‘Te eva pakirīyanti paṭṭhapīyanti ettha’ (they are scattered and established here or by this) means this is the treatise (pakaraṇa). The Vibhaṅga and that treatise together form the Vibhaṅgappakaraṇa. ‘By the illumination of the meaning of the word ādi’ (ādisaddatthajotakena) means by the clarifier of the meaning of the word ādi, as in phrases like ‘or, refraining from such things as dancing, singing, music, and seeing shows’ (Dīgha Nikāya 1.13). ‘By the illumination of the meaning of the mode’ (pakāratthajotakena) means by the clarifier of the meaning of the mode, as in phrases like ‘thus, monks, the fool is fearful, the wise one is fearless’ (Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.1). By ‘it indicates the whole by a part’ (ekadesena samudāyaṃ nidasseti) is shown the demonstrative function of the word ‘iti’ in phrases like ‘the aggregate of form… the aggregate of consciousness.’ For the word ‘iti’ is also seen to have a demonstrative meaning, as in ‘“It exists,” Kaccāna, this is one extreme’ (Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.15; 3.90). Or, it has a concluding meaning, as in ‘Therefore, monks, be heirs in the Dhamma, not heirs in material things. I have compassion for you, thinking, “How may my disciples be heirs in the Dhamma, not heirs in material things?”’ (Majjhima Nikāya 1.29). For this is a conclusion by showing a part of the discourse’s division, namely, ‘the five aggregates: the aggregate of form… the aggregate of consciousness,’ since the meaning is thereby summarized. ‘There’ (tattha) means in the Vibhaṅgappakaraṇa. Regarding ‘excluding Nibbāna’ (nibbānavajjānaṃ): If the analysis of the aggregates is stated first due to the aggregates being fewer in words (appakatarapadattā) among those excluding Nibbāna, then, since the truth analysis encompasses all phenomena including Nibbāna, and since it is fewer in words than the sense bases, etc., and the aggregates, which also encompass all phenomena, should not the analysis of the truths be stated first? No, because even there, in the analysis of the truth of suffering, only part of the aggregates is analyzed, as stated: ‘And what, monks, is the noble truth of suffering? Birth is suffering… in brief, the five aggregates subject to clinging are suffering’ (Vibhaṅga 190; Dīgha Nikāya 2.387; Majjhima Nikāya 1.120; 3.373). Here, however, the aggregates are analyzed without omission—thus, due to the aggregates being fewer in words compared to those excluding Nibbāna, the analysis of the aggregates is stated first.

entries.pali: 206-214 . ‘‘Pariññeyyabhāvarahite ekantapahātabbe’’ti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu taṇhāyapi cakkhādīnaṃ viya taṇhāvatthutāvacanena pariññeyyatā vuttā. Yathāha ‘‘rūpataṇhā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ, etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisatī’’tiādi (dī. ni. 2.400; ma. ni. 1.133; vibha. 203). Tappaṭibaddhasaṃkilesappahānavasena samatikkamitabbatā hi pariññeyyatā. Ekantapahātabbatā ca na taṇhāya eva, atha kho avasesānaṃ saṃkilesadhammānampi. Tathā hi tesaṃ sabbaso accantappahāyikā dassanabhāvanāti? Saccametaṃ, tathāpi yathā ‘‘dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pariññeyya’’nti (saṃ. ni. 5.1099) taṇhāvajje upādānakkhandhapañcake pariññeyyabhāvo niruḷho, na tathā taṇhāya, taṇhāya pana ‘‘yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobhavikā’’tiādinā (vibha. 203; dī. ni. 2.400; ma. ni. 1.91, 460; saṃ. ni. 5.1081; mahāva. 14; paṭi. ma. 1.34) samudayabhāvo viya sātisayaṃ pahātabbabhāvo niruḷhoti dassetuṃ ‘‘pariññeyyabhāvarahite ekantappahātabbe’’ ti vuttaṃ. Yassa asaṅgahito padeso atthi, so sappadeso, ekadesoti attho. Tatthā ti ariyasaccasadde. Samudayo ti samudayattho. ‘‘Nippadesato samudayaṃ dassetu’’nti samudayassevettha gahaṇe kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ ‘‘dukkhanirodhā panā’’ tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha dukkhanirodhā ti dukkhaṃ, nirodho ca. Ariyasaccadesanāya nti ariyasaccadesanāyampi saccadesanāyaṃ viya. Dhammato ti desetabbadhammato nippadesā eva. ‘‘Avasesā ca kilesā’’tiādinā desanābhedo eva hi tattha viseso. Tenāha ‘‘na hi tato añño’’ tiādi. Apubbo natthī ti dhammato apubbo natthīti attho. Tassā ti samudayassa. Sabbattha tīsupi vāresū ti aṭṭhaṅgikapañcaṅgikasabbasaṅgāhikabhedesu mahāvāresu, tadantogadhesu ca pañcasu koṭṭhāsesu. Apubbassā ti ‘‘avasesā ca kilesā’’tiādinā taṇhāya apubbassa. Avasiṭṭhakilesādīnañhi samudayatāvacanaṃ idha apubbadassanaṃ. Tassa yadipi dutiyatatiyavāresu viseso natthi, pañcasu pana koṭṭhāsesu uparūpari apubbaṃ dassitanti katvā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Tañhi samudayavisesadassanaṃ, itaraṃ pana maggavisesadassanaṃ. Tassa ca dhammato apubbābhāvo dassitoyeva. Yadi evaṃ dutiyādikoṭṭhāsesu, paṭhamakoṭṭhāsepi vā kasmā taṇhā gahitāti āha ‘‘apubbasamudayadassanatthāyapi hī’’ tiādi. Kevalāyā ti tadaññakilesādinirapekkhāya. Desanāvasena na vutto ti na dhammavasenāti adhippāyo. Tasmā dukkhādīni tattha ariyasaccadesanāyaṃ sappadesāni dassitāni honti pariyāyenāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Abhidhammadesanā pana nippariyāyakathāti katvā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ ‘‘nippadesato samudayaṃ dassetuṃ’’icceva vuttaṃ. Paccayasaṅkhāta nti paccayābhimataṃ paccayabhūtaṃ, paccayakoṭṭhāsaṃ vā.
entries.chinese_simplified: 206-214. 为什么说“于无遍知法，唯应断”呢？难道贪爱不像眼等那样，因其为贪爱之所依而被说为应遍知吗？如言：“世间之色爱，是可爱、可喜者，此贪生起时即于此生，安住时即于此住”等。遍知，实是通过断除与其相关的杂染而应超越的状态。而唯应断者，不仅是贪爱，也包括其余的杂染法。因为它们都需要通过见与修而完全、究竟地断除，不是吗？此言真实。然而，正如“苦圣谛应遍知”，遍知性是确立于除贪爱之外的五取蕴，而非贪爱。对于贪爱，则如“此爱能引后有”等，其作为集的状态，以及其尤应断除的状态已被确立，为显示此义，故说“于无遍知法，唯应断”。凡有未被摄入的部分，即为“有分”(sappadeso)，意为一部分。“于彼”(tatthāti)指于“圣谛”一词中。“集”(samudayoti)意为集之义。为显示此处取“集”的理由，而说“为无分地显示集”，又说“苦与灭……”等。其中，“苦灭”(dukkhanirodhāti)即苦与灭。“于圣谛教说中”(ariyasaccadesanāyanti)即在圣谛的教说中，也如在谛的教说中。从“法”(dhammato)而言，即从所应教之法而言，是无分的。“其余诸烦恼……”等，其差别仅在于教说之不同。因此说“实无异于彼……”等。“无新”(apubbo natthīti)意为从法而言无新。“彼”(tassāti)指集。“于所有三转中”(sabbattha tīsupi vāresūti)指于八支、五支、总摄等分别的大转中，以及包含于其中的五部分中。“新”(apubbassāti)指“其余诸烦恼……”等中，贪爱之新义。说其余烦恼等为集，于此是前所未有的开示。对此，虽然在第二、三转中无差别，但在五部分中则层层显示新义，故如是说。此实为显示集之差别，彼则为显示道之差别。其从法而言无新，此义已显示。若尔，在第二等部分中，为何在第一部分亦取贪爱？答曰：“亦为显示新集(apubbasamudaya)……”等。“唯”(kevalāyāti)指不依赖于其他烦恼等。“非由教说而说”，意为非由法而说。是故当知，苦等于圣谛教说中，是以有分(sappadesāni)的方式，即以方便(pariyāyenāti)而显示。阿毗达摩(abhidhamma)教说则是无方便说(nippariyāyakathā)，故义注(aṭṭhakathāyaṃ)中说“为无分地显示集”。“缘所成”(paccayasaṅkhātanti)指被认为是缘、作为缘者，或缘的部分。
entries.english: 206-214. Why is it said, 'devoid of the nature of what should be fully understood, to be entirely abandoned'? Is it not that craving, too, is to be fully understood, just like the eye and so on, since it is spoken of as a basis for craving? As it is said: 'Craving for forms—forms that are pleasant and delightful in the world—arises here when arising, and settles here when settling' (Dī. Ni. 2.400; Ma. Ni. 1.133; Vibha. 203). For, the nature of what is to be fully understood is that it is to be transcended by way of abandoning the defilements connected with it. And what is to be entirely abandoned is not craving alone, but the remaining defiled states as well. For is not their complete and final abandonment accomplished through seeing and development? This is true. Nevertheless, just as the nature of what is to be fully understood is established for the five aggregates of clinging, excluding craving, with the words, 'the noble truth of suffering is to be fully understood' (Saṃ. Ni. 5.1099), it is not so established for craving. Rather, for craving, its nature as what is to be abandoned is established with emphasis, like its nature as origin, by such phrases as 'this craving which leads to renewed existence' (Vibha. 203; etc.). To show this, it was said, 'devoid of the nature of what should be fully understood, to be entirely abandoned.' That which has an unincluded part is 'with a part,' meaning 'partial.' 'Therein' means in the term 'noble truth.' 'Origin' means the sense of origin. To show the reason for taking up 'origin' here completely, it is said, 'But suffering and cessation...' etc. Therein, 'suffering and cessation' means suffering and cessation. In the teaching of the noble truths, just as in the teaching of the truths, from the perspective of the phenomena to be taught, they are indeed complete. By 'and the remaining defilements,' etc., the distinction here is simply a difference in the teaching. Therefore, it is said, 'For there is none other than that,' etc. 'There is nothing unprecedented' means there is nothing unprecedented from the point of view of the phenomena. 'Of that' means of the origin. 'In all three sections' means in the great sections divided into the eightfold, fivefold, and all-inclusive, and in the five categories included within them. Regarding 'of the unprecedented': this refers to what is unprecedented in relation to craving, by way of 'and the remaining defilements,' etc. For the statement that the remaining defilements, etc., are the origin is what is shown as unprecedented here. Although there is no distinction in this regard in the second and third sections, it was said thus because in the five categories, what is unprecedented is shown successively. For that is the showing of the specifics of origin, while the other is the showing of the specifics of the path. And the absence of anything unprecedented from the point of view of the phenomena has indeed been shown. If so, in the second and following categories, or even in the first category, why is craving taken up? He says: 'For the purpose of showing the unprecedented origin...' etc. 'Of the sole [craving]' means independent of other defilements, etc. 'Not stated by way of teaching' means not by way of the phenomena; this is the intention. Therefore, it should be understood that suffering, etc., are shown there in the teaching of the noble truths as being 'with a part' by way of an indirect method. But since the Abhidhamma teaching is a direct discourse, it is said in the commentary, 'to show the origin completely.' 'Termed a condition' means what is intended as a condition, what has become a condition, or the category of conditions.

entries.pali: 46 . Cattāri ariyasaccāni – dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayo ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodho ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 46. 四圣谛(ariyasaccāni)：苦圣谛、苦集圣谛、苦灭圣谛、苦灭道圣谛。
entries.english: 46. Four Noble Truths: the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, and the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

entries.work_title: 阿毗达摩入门古复注 Abhidhammāvatāra-Purāṇaṭīkā
entries.pali: Cattāri ariyasaccāni pakāsetīti catusaccappakāsano . Dukkhasamudayanirodhamaggavasena hi cattāri ariyasaccāni. Yathāha, ‘‘cattārimāni, bhikkhave, ariyasaccāni. Katamāni cattāri? Dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasacca’’nti (saṃ. ni. 5.1083). Tattha tebhūmakā dhammā anekupaddavādhiṭṭhānatāya dhuvasubhādivirahena, kucchitatucchaṭṭhena ca dukkhaṃ nāma. Kammādivisesapaccayasamavāye dukkhuppattikāraṇabhāvena taṇhā samudayo nāma ‘‘samecca udeti dukkhaṃ imasmā’’ti katvā. Dukkhassa anuppādanirodhapaccayattā dukkhanirodho nibbānaṃ. Taṃ pana dukkhanirodhaṃ ālambaṇakaraṇavasena gamanato pāpuṇanato, tadadhigamāya paṭipadābhāvato cāti ‘‘dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’’ ti lokuttaramaggo vuccati. Saccaṭṭho pana tesaṃ tacchāviparītabhūtabhāvato veditabbo. Vuttañhi ‘‘‘idaṃ dukkhanti, bhikkhave, tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathameta’’nti (saṃ. ni. 5.1090) vitthāro. Ettha pana catunnaṃ ariyaphalānaṃ, ariyamaggasampayuttānañca saccavinissaṭabhāvepi idha magganibbānappakāsanatāvacaneneva tappakāsanatthampi vuttaṃ hoti, anāsavabhāvena ekalakkhaṇattā taṃtaṃhetukavisayabhāvato cāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 宣说四圣谛，故名‘四谛宣说者’。四圣谛即苦、集、灭、道。如所言：‘诸比丘，有此四圣谛。是哪四者？苦圣谛、苦集圣谛、苦灭圣谛、趣向苦灭之道圣谛。’(相应部 5.1083)。其中，三界诸法，因是诸多灾患之所依，远离常、净等，且义为空、贱，故名为‘苦’。渴爱，因在业等诸缘和合时，是苦生起之因，故名为‘集’，所谓‘苦由此和合而生’。作为苦不生、息灭之缘，故‘苦灭’即是涅槃。至于‘趣向苦灭之道’，因缘取苦灭，趣向、到达苦灭，且是证达苦灭之道，故出世间道被称为‘趣向苦灭之道’。其谛义，当知为真实、不颠倒、如是之状态。如所言：‘诸比丘，此是苦，此是真实，此非不实，此非他样。’(相应部 5.1090)此为广说。于此，虽四圣果及圣道相应法离于诸谛，然仅以于此宣说道与涅槃，亦已说及彼等之宣说。当知此因彼等同为无漏一相，且分别为彼彼之因与境故。
entries.english: He proclaims the Four Noble Truths; hence, he is the Proclaimer of the Four Truths (Catusaccappakāsano). For the Four Noble Truths are in terms of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. As it is said: ‘Bhikkhus, there are these Four Noble Truths. What four? The noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering’ (SN 56.11). Herein, the phenomena of the three planes are called suffering because they are the basis for many afflictions, are devoid of permanence, pleasure, etc., and have a contemptible and empty nature. Craving is called the origin because, through the convergence of specific conditions such as kamma, it is the cause for the arising of suffering, as it is said: ‘From this, suffering arises after coming together.’ The cessation of suffering is Nibbāna, as it is the condition for the non-arising and cessation of suffering. The supramundane path is called ‘the way leading to the cessation of suffering’ because one proceeds towards that cessation of suffering by way of making it an object and reaching it, and because it is the path for its attainment. The truth-nature of these should be understood from their being real, not unreal, and not otherwise. For it was said: ‘“This is suffering,” bhikkhus, this is real, this is not unreal, this is not otherwise’ (SN 56.20), and so on in detail. Here, although the four noble fruits and the factors associated with the noble path are distinct from the truths, by the very statement proclaiming the path and Nibbāna, the purpose of proclaiming them is also stated. This should be understood as being because they have a single characteristic in being untainted, and because they have their respective causes and objects.

entries.pali: Cattāri ariyasaccāni (vibha. 189) – dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccanti. Saccavibhaṅgaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 四圣谛（《分别论》189）——苦圣谛、苦集圣谛、苦灭圣谛、趣苦灭道圣谛。谛分别。
entries.english: The Four Noble Truths (Vibh. 189): the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, and the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. The Analysis of the Truths.
